answer.generated: The optimal number of processors is found by balancing parallelizable time against communication overhead. For each doubling of processors, communication costs increase by 0.5% of the original execution time. Thus, the speedup S is given by S = P / (P + 0.5 * log2(N)), where N is the number of processors. This equation shows that adding more processors beyond a certain point reduces speedup due to increasing communication costs, so the maximum speedup occurs when the communication overhead equals the parallelizable portion.
